claims.statement: SSHConnectionPreparation resolves a target plus ordered jump-hop configurations before transport opening, performs Keychain-dependent resolution in a cancellable detached task, and applies strict Known Hosts preparation or defers unknown-key approval according to the selected trust policy.

A configured proxy is attributed to its owning route host and is not a Journey endpoint: proxy connection and authentication remain on Local or the preceding SSH host, while only the next host SSH connection advances route progress.

SSH routing authenticates each jump on the current transport, opens a `direct-tcpip` bridge toward the next proxy or destination, and negotiates a following proxy over that bridge before the next SSH handshake.

Host-key authorization treats an external MD5 constraint only as an additional handshake constraint: a matching expected identity bypasses interaction, a conflicting known-host set still rejects, and an unknown identity requires an authorizer or fails closed.

Persistent Known Hosts trust is independent of Host records, while a Continue Once approval stays only in the live controller; persistent approval saves the key before resuming and disconnect rejects a pending decision and clears temporary keys.

SSH credentials and proxy/jump secrets are one-shot configuration material cleared at connection boundaries; interaction-forbidden requests remove interaction-dependent credentials and reject trust or prompted keyboard-interactive authentication.

`SSHConnection` serializes libssh2 calls through `SSHConnectionWorker`; worker cleanup increments a generation, cancels timers, fails commands, closes channel owners and the authenticated transport, preventing stale socket/timer work from affecting a retired connection.

Desktop restoration does not reconnect live Workspaces, whereas mobile persists only connection-free descriptors containing workspace ID, Host ID, kind and title; cold launch performs no session or network restoration. Mobile background expiration closes transports and foreground can resume existing workspace intent.

Telnet uses an independent direct-or-proxied TCP transport with generation-guarded callbacks, incremental Telnet negotiation and charset conversion, and consumes an automated password once; it is not an SSH trust, jump-host, or SFTP transport.

On desktop TermindApp shares one AppModel across scenes but constructs a WindowModel for each window; AppModel holds app-wide host services including an AgentHostServices resolver, authentication registry, connection pool and background-command owner, distinct from window-owned workspace sessions.

Agent host listing exposes public Vault metadata and temporary pane targets without credentials; temporary SSH configuration comes from a live desktop pane, and resolution fails when a temporary pane-backed target no longer exists.

Agent SSH authentication collects missing proxy and host credentials in route order before connecting; the attempt handles host-key and keyboard-interactive challenges during handshake, with permanent host-key trust allowed only for saved Hosts and one-shot approval held in the authentication context.

Overlapping Agent connections to the same host share a temporary authentication context and pending configuration/open; cancelling the last waiter cancels its prompt, stale generations cannot erase newer answers, and successful authentication clears staged secrets so unrelated later connections cannot reuse custom credentials.

AgentConnectionPool reuses an authenticated Host-ID-keyed connection across tools and runs according to a route fingerprint built without Keychain reads; route changes invalidate reuse, concurrent misses join an opening, and late cancelled openings are disconnected instead of committed.

The Agent pool multiplexes exec and primary SFTP over its own SSH connection, can obtain auxiliary or sibling SFTP channels, exempts active exec/SFTP leases from idle sweeping, and disconnects on host deletion or explicit app shutdown.

ssh_exec uses a non-PTY command channel with safe-command parallelism and approval for unproven commands; its deadline includes connection, returning connecting without starting a command if setup is still pending, or handing a running command to a background handle while retaining the pooled connection; only a pre-channel connection failure can be retried.

Desktop termination checks pending external edits, closes window-owned sessions and app services, waits for Assistant/MCP and SFTP drains before closing Agent background commands and connections, and answers the native termination request after cleanup or a three-second fallback.

When every mobile scene backgrounds, a UIKit background task is started; expiration synchronously requests workspace suspension, forwarding stop, transfer pause, and Assistant cancellation, then Assistant drains conversations before closing Agent background commands and pooled connections. Foreground ends the task and resumes only workspaces with recorded intent.

For an Agent connection through a proxy whose saved password identity is missing, the authentication card retains the proxy-configured username while clearing the unavailable identity selection; an unsaved proxy answer changes only the attempt, while a saved answer persists proxy identity and username to the host store.

When Agent authentication requires an identity followed by a protected-key passphrase, the passphrase response merges into the staged identity submission instead of replacing it, preserving any password fallback for that connection.

Closing the last desktop window does not necessarily terminate the application: the metrics menu preference and running metrics govern whether it quits, independently of the window-owned workspace transport lifetime.

A workspace trust approval resumes the pending live host-key handshake rather than opening a separate discovery connection; the feature pauses recovery while waiting and disconnect clears pending decisions.

Desktop terminal connection preparation is prompt-first rather than exclusively SSHConnectionPreparation-based: SSHSessionModel resolves per-attempt staged proxy, host, key/passphrase and username requirements, builds the target and jump configuration from the host store, and routes credential errors to the failing hop or proxy before retrying.

The desktop terminal checks attempt identity before installing a connected PTY and on asynchronous exit callbacks, and disconnects the new actor when installation fails; explicit disconnect cancels the task and trust/reconnect state and discards staged secrets.

Desktop AppModel.open configures per-window connection-history callbacks, sets an optimistic terminal status and delegates pane/workspace creation to WindowModel; HostLibraryModel aggregates per-connection status so an online sibling remains connected when another pane fails or closes.

Desktop connection history is recorded when a saved-host pane opens, not when authentication succeeds, and is ended when the pane closes; source device identity, kind, latest-event recents and local-only filtering do not depend on a successful transport.

On mobile new live workspaces are published and eligible descriptors saved before connecting; a saved Host workspace gets one active connection-history entry until explicit close, while transient external-link workspaces have neither persisted descriptors nor saved-host history and opening an already-live descriptor does not reconnect.

ConnectionHistoryTests cover sorted repeated attempts, global 250-entry retention, persisted history clearing, source-device filtering, end-on-desktop-pane-close, saved SSH/SFTP recents and clearing a host's history without deleting its Host or other hosts' events.

ConnectionHistoryModel trims the global history to 250 attempts on initialization and insertion, and reports repository failures as storageError rather than returning a successfully recorded event; local recents exclude records without the current stable source-device ID.

On mobile, loading recent workspaces prunes descriptors whose saved Host no longer exists; an invalid or unreadable workspace snapshot blocks subsequent saves instead of overwriting the original bytes, and cold launch creates no live sessions.

When all mobile scenes background, MobileAppModel pauses synchronization, metrics and outbox and disables external-edit monitoring; on an active scene it finishes the background task, rechecks edits, resumes intent-bearing workspaces and restarts or reconciles those services.
